issues.t: Transmission slips, flares or shifts harshly
issues.sym: Engine revs flare between gears, the car slips or shudders pulling away, shifts are harsh or erratic, and the check engine light may show P1811 or P0748.
issues.why: GM bulletin 00-07-30-002B covers this group of symptoms in the 4T65-E automatic. Code P0748 points to the pressure control solenoid, and worn valve body parts cause similar shifts.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have the codes read early, because a solenoid or valve body repair caught before the clutches burn can avoid a rebuilt transmission.

issues.t: Transmission drops into neutral at highway speed
issues.sym: At highway speed or in fourth gear, the car suddenly loses drive as if it shifted into neutral, then may catch again.
issues.why: GM bulletin 677164 calls for replacing the transmission control valve body to cure intermittent loss of drive in the 4T60-E.
issues.next: If it loses drive, signal, move to the shoulder and stop. Don't keep driving it on the highway; have a transmission shop check for the valve body bulletin.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak
issues.sym: Red fluid spots under the front of the car and a falling transmission fluid level.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover oil leaks from the 4T65-E transaxle, including fluid pushing out of the breather vent and leaking gaskets.
issues.next: Check the fluid with the engine warm and keep it full. Running low causes slipping and damage, so have the leak fixed.

issues.t: Oil pan leak that keeps coming back
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine and a burning oil smell, even after the oil pan gasket was already replaced.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01-06-01-008 covers repeat oil pan leaks on the 3.8L V6 and a revised repair.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped off. Have the pan resealed using the updated procedure, not just tightened.

issues.t: Oil leak at the rear of the engine
issues.sym: Oil leaking from where the engine meets the transmission, usually on the driver's side.
issues.why: The rear main crankshaft seal can leak. GM issued a bulletin on this leak and later a new seal and installation tool.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. A slow leak can wait, but a fast one needs fixing before the engine runs low. Rule out the simpler oil pan gasket first.

issues.t: Coolant leak near the throttle body
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, or crusty residue around the throttle body at the top of the engine.
issues.why: GM bulletin 01-06-01-007A covers coolant leaks at the upper intake manifold near the throttle body; the intake material can break down.
issues.next: Keep coolant full and watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs into the red, pull over and shut the engine off. Have the intake leak repaired before it causes overheating.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or fails
issues.sym: Coolant dripping near the front of the engine, a whining or grinding noise, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: Owners reported water pump failures around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If the engine overheats, stop and turn it off. Replace a leaking pump before it fails completely.

issues.t: Rusted floor under the battery
issues.sym: Rust holes in the floor under the rear seat, where the battery sits, sometimes with water getting in.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins on rust eating through the floor pan in the battery compartment.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the battery compartment and the floor around it. Have rust repaired before it spreads or the battery comes loose.

issues.t: Rusted front subframe
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, or rust holes found in the front cradle that holds the engine and suspension.
issues.why: An owner reported the front cradle rusting through. On older cars driven in salted areas, frame rust is common.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift, especially in snowbelt states. A badly rusted cradle can let suspension parts shift, so don't ignore it.

issues.t: Transaxle growl for a few minutes after starting
issues.sym: A growling noise from the transmission area during the first few minutes after a start, which goes away when warm.
issues.why: GM bulletin 10001 covers this transaxle growl in the first four minutes after startup.
issues.next: If it fades as the car warms up, it is usually not urgent. Mention the bulletin if you have it checked.

issues.t: Grinding noise in Park on a hill
issues.sym: Grinding or growling from the transmission when parked on a slope with the engine running.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-07-30-030 covers this noise in the 4T60-E family of transaxles.
issues.next: Use the parking brake before shifting into Park on hills. Mention the bulletin if you have it checked.

issues.t: Steering moans when parking
issues.sym: A moan, shudder or vibration in the steering when turning the wheel slowly at parking-lot speed.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-02-32-007 covers power steering moan during parking moves on dry pavement.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. If it is full, a shop can flush the fluid or apply the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Shake or vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: A shake through the steering wheel, floor and seat at highway speed on smooth roads.
issues.why: GM bulletins on this car point to tire and wheel balance and uniformity as the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the tires road-force balanced and checked for damage or uneven wear.

issues.t: Chuggle or surge on light throttle
issues.sym: A slight chugging or surging when accelerating gently or cruising at highway speed, with no warning light.
issues.why: GM bulletin 05-06-04-058 covers this chuggle with no trouble codes.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check for the bulletin. Make sure the spark plugs, wires and fuel injectors are in good shape.

issues.t: ABS or traction control light on
issues.sym: The ABS or traction control light stays on, and anti-lock braking or traction control may not work.
issues.why: Owners report ABS module and modulator faults and water-related sensor problems. GM bulletin 10004 also covers ABS and traction lights with codes.
issues.next: Normal braking usually still works, but wheels can lock in a hard stop. Drive carefully and have the codes read.

issues.t: Front brake noise
issues.sym: Squeal, grinding or groan from the front brakes when you press the pedal.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins on front brake noise for these cars.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors checked. Grinding usually means the pads are worn out, so don't wait.

issues.t: Won't start because of the anti-theft key
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or won't crank, and a security light may be on.
issues.why: The key has a chip that the anti-theft system reads. When the key, the ignition cylinder or its wiring wears, the system may stop recognizing the key.
issues.next: Try a spare key. If it still won't start, a shop can check the key resistance and ignition cylinder wiring.

issues.t: Trunk lid won't close all the way
issues.sym: The trunk won't latch and pull itself shut.
issues.why: The power pull-down switch for the trunk can fail.
issues.next: Close the trunk firmly and make sure it latched. Replace the pull-down switch or motor.

issues.t: Heated seat stops warming
issues.sym: The heated seat back or cushion no longer warms up.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-08-50-021 covers failed heating elements in the front seats.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. A shop can replace the heating element.

issues.t: Fuel smell from leaking fuel lines or tank
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell, fuel dripping or spraying under the car, or a puddle where you park.
issues.why: Owners reported pinholes in the plastic fuel lines and fuel tanks rusting through and splitting.
issues.next: Don't drive the car if you smell gas or see a leak, and keep sparks and flames away. Have it towed and the lines or tank replaced.

issues.t: Engine dies at highway speed
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, sometimes on the highway, and may not restart right away.
issues.why: Owners reported stalling that dealers could not always reproduce. Possible causes include a failing ignition part, engine sensor or fuel pump.
issues.next: Steer to safety; steering and brakes get heavy with the engine off. Have the codes read and the ignition and fuel systems tested.

issues.t: Engine backfire can crack the intake (recall)
issues.sym: A backfire while starting, followed by a no-start. In rare cases it can start an engine compartment fire.
issues.why: A backfire on startup could break the upper intake manifold. GM recall 96V116000 updated the engine computer.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Until it is done, keep the hood shut when starting the car, as the recall advised.

issues.t: Seat belt and key chimes may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No chime when the key is left in or the driver's belt is unbuckled; interior lights or power locks may act up.
issues.why: A damaged capacitor in the body control module (called the MALL module). GM recall 95V204000.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. A Buick dealer inspects and replaces the module free.

issues.t: Seat belt won't latch or retract
issues.sym: A front buckle won't latch, or a rear belt won't pull back in and stays slack.
issues.why: Owners reported failed buckles and weak rear retractors. NHTSA opened an investigation into the rear seat belt retractor.
issues.next: Don't carry a passenger in a seat whose belt doesn't latch and lock. Have the buckle or retractor replaced.

issues.t: Steering column loose or clicking
issues.sym: The steering column feels loose or moves, the tilt won't hold, or there is a snap or click when turning.
issues.why: Owners reported loose tilt bolts. A GM bulletin covers a snap or click from the column when turning.
issues.next: A loose column needs prompt attention. Have the column bolts and tilt mechanism checked.

issues.t: Battery runs down over a few days
issues.sym: The battery goes flat if the car sits for a few days.
issues.why: Something stays powered after the car is shut off. This is the most reported 1996 Riviera problem on CarComplaints.
issues.next: Have the battery tested, then have a shop do a parasitic draw test to find the circuit draining it.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working
issues.sym: The front or rear power door locks don't work.
issues.why: A GM bulletin covers power door locks that stop working.
issues.next: Check the fuse first. A shop can then replace the faulty lock actuator or switch.

issues.t: Clunk or rattle from the front over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, rattle or metal-on-metal noise from the front end on rough roads.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-03-08-005 covers front-end clunk and rattle noises.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected for worn links, mounts or loose parts.

issues.t: Popping noise inside the car
issues.sym: A popping noise heard in the passenger compartment.
issues.why: GM bulletin 99-06-05-005 covers this noise.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. A shop can apply the bulletin fix.
